style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;resizable=0;points=[];autosize=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;" value="<font style="font-size:12px">1. Threads in same <b>warp</b> → execute in lockstep (same instruction, same cycle)<br>2. Threads in same <b>block</b> → CAN share data and synchronize<br>3. style="color:#4ade80;">✓</td><td>Same <b style="color:#93c5fd">block</b> → CAN share data (<code>__shared__</code>) and synchronize (<code>__syncthreads</code>)</td></tr><tr><td style="color:#f87171;">✗</td><td>Different <b style="color:#93c5fd">blocks</b> → CANNOT share data, CANNOT synchronize, execute in ANY order</td></tr><tr><td style="color:#4ade80;">✓</td><td>One <b style="color:#c4b5fd">block</b> lives on one <b style="color:#c4b5fd">SM</b> — never split. This enables shared memory.</td></tr><tr><td style="color:#4ade80;">✓</td><td>More threads than cores is GOOD — enables latency hiding via warp switching</td></tr><tr><td style="color:#4ade80;">✓</td><td>Kernel launch is ASYNCHRONOUS — CPU continues immediately, use <code>cudaDeviceSynchronize()</code> to wait</td></tr><tr><td style="color:#fbbf24;">!</td><td>CUDA errors are SILENT — always check with <code>cudaGetLastError()</code></td></tr></table></font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="850" x="65" y="1170" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="int n = 10000;<br>int size = n * sizeof(float); —> 40,000 bytes<br><br><i>Why: the GPU driver and malloc() only understand raw byte counts, not &quot;elements&quot; — so every allocation converts element-count × sizeof(type) into bytes up front.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="500" x="70" y="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-25" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="Allocate HOST memory:<br>A_h = (float*)malloc(size);<br>B_h = (float*)malloc(size);<br>C_h = (float*)malloc(size);<br><br><i>Why: these live in ordinary CPU RAM (the process heap). malloc() only knows about bytes, so the <b>(float*)</b> cast tells the compiler how to interpret and index that raw block as an array of floats.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="500" x="70" y="440" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-26" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;A_h[i] = 1.0f;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;B_h[i] = 2.0f;<br>}<br><i>Why: C_h is deliberately left uninitialized (garbage) here — it exists only to receive the GPU's answer later. If verification ran before vecAdd(), C_h would contain junk.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="500" x="70" y="600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-27" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;strokeWidth=2;" value="vecAdd(A_h, B_h, C_h, n);<br><i>A normal, synchronous C function call — main() halts here and waits for vecAdd() to fully return before continuing (unlike a kernel launch).</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="500" x="70" y="770" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-28" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="int correct = 1;<br>for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;if (C_h[i] != 3.0f) {<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;printf("Error at index %d..."); correct=0; break;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;}<br>}<br><i>Why 3.0f exactly (no epsilon/tolerance needed): 1.0f + 2.0f is exactly representable in IEEE-754 float — no rounding error, so a strict != comparison is safe here.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="160" width="500" x="70" y="900" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-29" parent="1" style="rhombus;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#cde2fb;strokeColor=#2a78d6;fontColor=#0b0b0b;fontSize=12;fontStyle=1;" value="correct == 1 ?" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="200" x="220" y="1100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-30" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="printf("SUCCESS - All %d elements are correct.", n);" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="500" x="70" y="1230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-31" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="free(A_h);<br>free(B_h);<br>free(C_h);<br><br><i>Why: releases the CPU heap memory back to the OS. Note there is nothing to free on the device here — vecAdd() already cudaFree'd A_d/B_d/C_d before it returned.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="500" x="70" y="1330" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-32" parent="1" style="shape=terminator;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=13;fontStyle=1;" value="return 0; — End" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="200" x="220" y="1500" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-33" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;strokeWidth=2;" value="vecAdd(A_h, B_h, C_h, n) — HOST function entry<br><br>Runs entirely on the CPU. Its only job is to <b>drive</b> the GPU: allocate device memory → copy inputs in → launch the kernel → copy the result back → free device memory." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="500" x="690" y="220" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-34" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="<b>Part 1 — Setup</b><br>float *A_d, *B_d, *C_d;<br><br><i>Why: these are just pointer VARIABLES sitting in CPU stack memory. Right now they are uninitialized — they will hold GPU (device) addresses only after cudaMalloc runs. The <b>_d</b> suffix (device) vs <b>_h</b> (host) is a naming convention, not a language rule — it's how the programmer tracks which memory space each pointer is valid in.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="500" x="690" y="410" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-35" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="int size = n * sizeof(float);<br><i>Recomputed locally — vecAdd() only received n, not the byte size main() already computed.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="500" x="690" y="600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-36" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="cudaMalloc((void**)&A_d, size);<br>cudaMalloc((void**)&B_d, size);<br>cudaMalloc((void**)&C_d, size);<br><br><i>Why (void**): cudaMalloc must WRITE the new GPU address into your pointer variable. To modify a variable through a function call, C needs the address OF that variable — i.e. a pointer to the pointer. It's typed void** because cudaMalloc is type-agnostic; the cast tells the compiler to accept any pointer type there. Each call reserves <b>size</b> bytes in DEVICE GLOBAL MEMORY (VRAM) — completely separate physical RAM from the host.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="500" x="690" y="720" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-37" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="cudaMemcpy(A_d, A_h, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);<br>cudaMemcpy(B_d, B_h, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);<br><br><i>Why: host (CPU) and device (GPU) have physically separate DRAM. The GPU cannot reach into main()'s heap on its own — every byte has to be explicitly shipped across the PCIe bus. C_h/C_d are NOT copied here: there is no output yet, and copying it would be wasted bandwidth.<br>(see the Memory Map diagram below)</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="500" x="690" y="960" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-38" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="<b>Part 2 — Kernel Launch Configuration</b><br>int threadsPerBlock = 256;<br>int blocksPerGrid = (n + threadsPerBlock - 1) / threadsPerBlock;<br>= (10000 + 255) / 256 = <b>40</b><br><br><i>Why the &quot;+255&quot;: plain integer division n/256 TRUNCATES (10000/256 = 39.06 → 39), which would drop the last 16 elements entirely. Adding (threadsPerBlock-1) before dividing forces a round-UP (ceiling) division, guaranteeing every element gets a thread even when n is not an exact multiple of 256.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="500" x="690" y="1200" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-39" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;strokeWidth=2;" value="vecAddKernel&lt;&lt;&lt;blocksPerGrid, threadsPerBlock&gt;&gt;&gt;(A_d, B_d, C_d, n);<br><i>(async — this line returns to the CPU immediately)</i><br><br><i>Why: &lt;&lt;&lt;grid, block&gt;&gt;&gt; is CUDA's launch syntax — here it means &quot;create 40 blocks of 256 threads&quot; = 10,240 threads, all running the same kernel code. Launching is asynchronous: the CPU queues the work and moves on to the next C++ statement without waiting.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="500" x="690" y="1460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-40" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#4a3aa7;strokeColor=#382b80;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;strokeWidth=2;" value="cudaMemcpy(C_h, C_d, size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);<br><br><i>Why this line BLOCKS: on the default stream, cudaMemcpy is implicitly synchronizing — the CPU stalls here until every one of the 10,240 threads launched above has finished, THEN the driver copies the finished C_d buffer back across PCIe into C_h.<br>(see the Memory Map diagram below)</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="500" x="690" y="1680" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="2SuehunaCLx9PeHquNYd-41" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#2a78d6;strokeColor=#184f95;fontColor=#ffffff;fontSize=12;arcSize=6;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="<b>Part 3 — Cleanup</b><br>cudaFree(A_d);<br>cudaFree(B_d);<br>cudaFree(C_d);<br><br><i>Why: returns the three device allocations to the GPU's memory pool. Skipping this would leak VRAM for the lifetime of the process (or until the CUDA context is destroyed).</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="500" x="690" y="1900" as="geometry" /> all launched threads) — they exist only because grid size must be a whole number of blocks.<br><br><i>If blocksPerGrid instead used plain truncating division (n/threadsPerBlock = 39, no +255), only 39×256 = 9,984 threads would launch, covering i = 0..9983. The last <b>16 elements (indices 9984..9999) would never be computed</b> — C_h[9984..9999] would stay uninitialized garbage and the verification loop in main() would report an error. div.div: Three parts of this one file: (1) __global__ vecAddKernel — the parallel program that EVERY GPU thread executes (Device). (2) vecAdd() — a normal C function that runs on the CPU and orchestrates the whole GPU workflow: allocate device memory → copy inputs in → launch the kernel → copy the result back → free device memory (Host). (3) main() — allocates/initializes the data, calls vecAdd() once, then verifies every result (Host).

div.div:
vecAdd(A_h, B_h, C_h, n) — HOST function entry
Runs entirely on the CPU. Its only job is to drive the GPU: allocate device memory → copy inputs in → launch the kernel → copy the result back → free device memory.

Grid = 40 blocks × Block = 256 threads/block
= 10,240 threads created
(only 10,000 elements exist — 240 will be idle)

div.div:
Every thread runs the SAME instructions (SIMT)
vecAddKernel(A_d, B_d, C_d, n)
independently, at (mostly) the same time

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(235, 104, 52), rgb(219, 106, 62)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(138, 52, 19), rgb(239, 165, 136));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 510px; height: 1px; padding-top: 781px; margin-left: 1281px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #ffffff;

div.div:
int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
blockIdx.x: which block this thread lives in (0..39)
blockDim.x: threads per block, fixed at 256
threadIdx.x: this thread's slot inside its block (0..255)
Why: this formula flattens the 2-level hardware hierarchy (block, thread) into ONE global index, so all 10,240 threads get a unique i in [0, 10239] mapping onto the flat 1-D arrays A/B/C.

div.div:
C[i] = A[i] + B[i];
Reads A_d[i], B_d[i] from device global memory, adds them, writes the sum into C_d[i]. This is the ONLY line of actual work in the whole program.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(227, 73, 72), rgb(250, 118, 117)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(161, 42, 42), rgb(255, 158, 158));

div.div:
Do nothing — thread exits.
Guards against reading/writing past index 9999 into memory the GPU never allocated for A/B/C.

div.div: Kernel instance retires (thread finishes)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 248, 225), rgb(30, 24, 4)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(212, 160, 23), rgb(143, 98, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 510px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1496px; margin-left: 1281px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #52514e;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#52514e, #a7a7a4); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why the "if (i < n)" guard is essential:
blocksPerGrid was rounded UP to 40 (not 39.06), so the LAST block (blockIdx.x = 39) covers global indices i = 39×256 .. 39×256+255 = 9984 .. 10239 — but the arrays only hold 10,000 valid elements (indices 0..9999).
Without this check, the 240 threads with i ≥ 10000 would read/write past the end of the cudaMalloc'd buffers — undefined behavior, silent memory corruption, or a crash. The guard simply lets those threads do nothing.

div.div: Discrete GPU memory model: the CPU and GPU have separate physical DRAM. A pointer valid in one address space is meaningless (or a crash) in the other — you cannot dereference A_h on the GPU, nor A_d on the CPU. This is exactly why the code keeps two parallel sets of pointers (_h = host, _d = device) and why every transfer needs an explicit cudaMemcpy call — there is no automatic mirroring between them.

div.div:
Total threads created = blocksPerGrid × threadsPerBlock = 40 × 256 = 10,240
Elements actually needed = n = 10,000
Idle / guarded threads = 240 (≈2.3% of all launched threads) — they exist only because grid size must be a whole number of blocks.
If blocksPerGrid instead used plain truncating division (n/threadsPerBlock = 39, no +255), only 39×256 = 9,984 threads would launch, covering i = 0..9983. The last 16 elements (indices 9984..9999) would never be computed — C_h[9984..9999] would stay uninitialized garbage and the verification loop in main() would report an error. The ceiling-division "+threadsPerBlock-1" trick exists specifically to prevent that.
